newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil eyes $2 bln in World Bank loans - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil eyes $2 bln in World Bank loans - paper.

text.p: Brazil is negotiating for some $2 billion in World Bank loans for the fiscal year starting July 1997, part of which will be used to clean up state finances, a local newspaper said.
Jornal do Brasil said a World Bank mission lead by Gobin Nankani, director of the bank's Latin America and Caribbean department, was in Brasilia last week meeting with Planning Ministry officials.

The paper said Rio de Janeiro state is in the final stages of negotiations with the World Bank for a $300 million loan for a railroad project while Rio Grande do Sul state hopes to garner a $150 million loan for financial restructuring.
